newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indosat says Cambodia unit to meet target.
newsitem.headline: Indosat says Cambodia unit to meet target.

text.p: Indonesia's state-controlled PT Indonesian Satellite Corporation (Indosat) said on Monday it expected its Cambodian telecommunications unit Camintel, S.A. to reach the break-even point in 1998 or 1999 despite the country teetering on the brink of civil war.
"We expect the firm to reach the break-even point either in 1998 or 1999 despite the latest political developments," investor relations manager Budi Prasetyo told Reuters.
New York-listed Indosat owns a 49-percent stake in Camintel, Cambodia's domestic and international telephone operator, while the Cambodian government owns the rest, Prasetyo said.
Prasetyo said Indosat remained committed to its Cambodian investment and that the spirit of ASEAN (Association of South East Asian Nations) solidarity should help defuse tension in the country.
"Camintel started operations early this year. It is still a loss-making firm," Prasetyo said. He declined to give further details.
ASEAN, which links Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam, is scheduled to induct Cambodia into the grouping later this month.
Indosat is the major Indonesian investor in Cambodia.
